findings.title: Materials' forward P/E hides a 127% earnings bet
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.36x forward but 37.15x trailing, a 65-point percentile gap between the two lenses. The market is underwriting a 127 percent earnings surge that would be the steepest in the table, yet the forward multiple sits at percentile 23 — cheap only if that growth actually arrives.

findings.title: Real Estate's collapse is a de-rating, not an earnings story
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile fell 63 points in a month to 8, while its forward P/E of 34.25 remains the highest of any sector. The multiple barely moved relative to that percentile plunge, meaning the selloff is compressing the earnings base itself — implied growth is a 4 percent decline, so investors are paying a premium for shrinking profits.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' cheapness is a month-old panic
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile dropped 39 points in a month to 12, yet its trailing percentile sits at 59 — a 47-point gap. That divergence says the market is pricing in a 39 percent earnings rebound, but the speed of the de-rating looks like a sentiment shock rather than a fundamental repricing.
